extDescription.message: HTTP request redirection, blocking and mocking, header modification and an API client. No servers, accounts or telemetry.
extDescription.description: Store and extensions page description. At most 132 characters.

popupTagline.message: HTTP request redirection, blocking and modification. All data is stored locally in the browser.

navLabel.description: Accessible name of the sidebar navigation.

policyDescription.message: Settings set by your organization's administrator through enterprise browser policy (managed storage). They take precedence over user settings and cannot be edited in the extension.

policyEmptyText.message: No organization restrictions apply. All features are available, and all settings are user-defined.

policyIssues.message: The policy contains errors. Invalid restrictions fall back to their strictest form, and other invalid values are ignored.

policyNoHosts.message: None (access to all sites is blocked)

policyUserRulesForbidden.message: Not allowed (only organization rules and mocks apply)

transferDescription.message: Transfer rules, mocks and environments between browsers and users as a JSON file (easy to keep in git).

transferExportHint.message: Organization policy records and secret values are not exported (secret variables are exported by name only).

transferImportHint.message: Records with a matching id replace existing ones, and nothing is deleted. Secret values in this browser and policy records stay unchanged.

transferCounts.description: $1 is a list such as Rules; $2, $3 and $4 are numbers.

transferImportFailed.description: $1 is the technical reason, in English.

interceptionOn.message: Enabled rules and mocks apply on allowed sites.

interceptionOff.message: Interception paused (rules and mocks are not applied).

interceptionPaused.message: Interception is paused. Rules are not applied.

interceptionSaveFailed.message: Failed to toggle interception. Try again.

rulesDescription.message: Redirect and block requests, modify their headers. If several rules match a request, the one higher in the list applies. Header modification rules all apply, and for the same header the rule higher in the list takes precedence.

rulesNoSites.message: Add allowed sites to apply rules. The list of allowed sites is currently empty.

rulesPolicyOnly.message: The organization policy allows only organization rules. User rules are not applied.

rulesFeaturesOff.message: Disabled by the organization policy: $1. Rules of these types are not applied.
rulesFeaturesOff.description: $1 is a list of features, such as Redirection, Blocking.

rulesEmptyText.message: Request redirection and blocking, header modification by URL pattern.

rulesActionFailed.message: Failed to update the rule. Try again.

ruleNoAccess.message: Requestion has no host permission for $1, so the rule is not applied there.
ruleNoAccess.description: $1 is a host name, such as api.example.com.

ruleHostNotAllowed.message: The organization policy blocks access to $1, so the rule is not applied there.
ruleHostNotAllowed.description: $1 is a host name, such as api.example.com.

ruleBadgeRedirect.description: Short name of the action in the rule list.

ruleBadgeHeaders.description: Short name of the action in the rule list.

ruleBadgeBlock.description: Short name of the action in the rule list.

ruleSummaryRedirect.description: $1 is the redirect target, such as a URL.

ruleSummaryTransform.description: $1 lists the changed parts, such as Port: 8080.

ruleSummaryHeaders.description: $1 lists header names, such as X-Debug, Cookie.

rulesSaveFailed.description: $1 is the technical reason, in English.

rulesDeleteText.message: The rule “$1” will be permanently deleted.

ruleTypeRedirectHint.message: Redirects matching requests to another URL.

ruleTypeHeadersHint.message: Sets, appends or removes headers of matching requests and their responses.

ruleTypeBlockHint.message: Matching requests are cancelled before reaching the network (net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT).

rulePatternFilterHint.message: || — start of a domain, * — any characters, ^ — separator (for example, / or ?).

rulePatternRegexHint.message: RE2 syntax (used by Chrome). Capture groups can be substituted into the redirect URL.

patternFilterEdge.message: anchor (start or end of the URL)

patternFilterSeparator.message: separator (any character except letters, digits and _ - . %) or the end of the URL

patternFilterExampleSite.message: any request to example.com and its subdomains

patternRegexExampleGroup.message: the part after /v1/ is captured in group \1 (for redirect substitution)

patternRegexExampleWww.message: http and https schemes, with or without the www subdomain

patternRegexExampleId.message: URLs ending with /users/ and a numeric ID

patternRegexNote.message: The expression is matched against the full URL (including the scheme). Escape dots (\.). RE2 does not support lookarounds or backreferences.

ruleMethodsHint.message: If none are selected, all methods match.

ruleResourceTypesHint.message: If none are selected, all types match, including top-level documents (main_frame).

ruleInitiatorDomainsHint.message: Domains of the pages that send the request, comma-separated (including subdomains).

redirectExampleUrl.message: All matching requests are redirected to this exact URL. The path and query string of the original URL are not preserved.

redirectExampleSubstitution.message: The pattern captures the rest of the URL in group \1, and the substitution inserts it into the new URL (/users?page=2 is preserved as /users?page=2).

redirectExampleTransform.message: Only the filled-in URL parts change (in this example, the host). The path and query string are preserved.

ruleSubstitutionHint.message: \1–\9 — capture groups of the regular expression.

ruleSubstitutionNeedsRegex.message: Substitution requires capture groups from a regular expression. Set the pattern syntax to Regular expression.

ruleTransformHint.message: Empty fields keep the corresponding part of the original URL.

ruleHeaderDelete.description: Accessible name of the × button in a header row.

sitesDescription.message: Requestion acts only on allowed sites. The browser checks access to both the request host and the initiator page. Mocks apply only on sites where they are turned on.

sitesDomainPlaceholder.description: Sample domain in an empty input. Not translated.

sitesEmptyText.message: Enter a domain above. The browser will request access confirmation.

sitesWithSubdomains.description: Badge next to a domain whose subdomains are allowed too.

sitesInvalidDomain.message: Enter a valid domain (for example, example.com or localhost).

sitesNotAllowed.message: The organization policy blocks access to this site.

sitesSubdomainsNotAllowed.message: The organization policy allows this site without subdomains. Clear the Include subdomains checkbox.

sitesAllowedHosts.message: The organization policy allows access only to: $1.
sitesAllowedHosts.description: $1 is a list of hosts, such as example.com, *.example.org.

sitesNoHostsAllowed.message: The organization policy blocks access to all sites.

sitesRequestFailed.message: Failed to request access. Try again.

sitesRemoveFailed.message: Failed to revoke access. Try again.

sitesMocksFailed.message: Failed to toggle mocks for the site. Try again.

mocksDescription.message: Replace responses to fetch and XHR requests. If several mocks match a request, the one higher in the list applies. Changes apply to open pages after a reload.

mocksPaused.message: Interception is paused. Mocks are not applied.

mocksNoSites.message: Turn on mocks for a site to apply them. Mocks are currently off on all sites.

mocksPolicyOnly.message: The organization policy allows only organization mocks. User mocks are not applied.

mocksFeatureOff.message: Mock API is disabled by the organization policy. Mocks are not applied.

mocksSecretsWarning.message: Mocks are readable by page scripts. Do not store tokens, passwords or other secrets in them.

mocksEmptyText.message: Response mocking (status, headers, body) by URL pattern.

mocksActionFailed.message: Failed to update the mock. Try again.

mocksSaveFailed.description: $1 is the technical reason, in English.

mocksDeleteText.message: The mock “$1” will be permanently deleted.

mockSummaryMethods.description: $1 is a list of HTTP methods.

mockDelayHint.message: Up to 60,000 ms. If empty, the response is returned without delay.

mockBodyHint.message: A JSON body must be valid JSON. Responses with null body statuses (for example, 204) have no body.

mockHeadersEmpty.message: Without headers, the response includes only a Content-Type matching the body format.

settingsDescription.message: Requestion interface settings for this browser.

languageEnglish.description: Language name in that language. Not translated.

languageRussian.description: Language name in that language. Not translated.

settingsPrivacy.message: Rules and settings are stored locally in this browser. Requestion uses no servers, accounts or telemetry.

settingsSaveFailed.message: Failed to save the setting. Try again.

apiClientDisabledTitle.message: API client is disabled by the organization policy

apiClientDisabledText.message: Your organization's administrator disabled it through enterprise browser policy. Request history is preserved.

apiClientNewTab.description: Title of a request tab while its URL is empty.

apiClientTabClose.description: $1 is the title of the tab: a URL or “New request”.

apiClientParamsEmpty.message: Parameters are appended to the URL query string, after existing ones.

apiClientHeadersEmpty.message: The browser adds some headers automatically (for example, Accept and User-Agent).

apiClientRuleHeaders.message: Headers forbidden for fetch() are set by a temporary declarativeNetRequest rule for this request only: $1. A Cookie header replaces the site's cookies.
apiClientRuleHeaders.description: $1 is a comma-separated list of header names.

apiClientBrowserHeaders.message: These headers are set by the browser, so the values entered here are not sent: $1.
apiClientBrowserHeaders.description: $1 is a comma-separated list of header names.

apiClientFieldsEmpty.message: The form is sent as application/x-www-form-urlencoded.

apiClientBodyNoneHint.message: The request is sent without a body.

apiClientContentTypeHint.message: Sent as the Content-Type header unless set explicitly in the headers.

apiClientBodyless.message: $1 requests are sent without a body. The body is kept for other methods.

apiClientSendCookiesHint.message: Off: the request is sent without site cookies (credentials: omit). On: the browser adds all site cookies, including the current session cookies (credentials: include).

apiClientResponseIdle.message: The response appears here after the request is sent.

apiClientResponseBinary.description: $1 is the content type, such as image/png.

apiClientResponseCookiesNote.message: The Set-Cookie header is not shown because the browser hides it from fetch() (forbidden response header).

apiClientInvalidRequest.description: $1 is the technical reason, in English.

apiClientSendFailed.description: $1 is what the browser reported, in English.

apiClientTimedOut.message: The full response was not received within $1 s (timeout). The request was aborted.

apiClientResponseTruncated.message: The response exceeds $1, so only the beginning was downloaded.
apiClientResponseTruncated.description: $1 is a size such as 10 MB.

apiClientSendFailedHint.message: Possible causes: the server is down or unreachable, or the browser does not trust its TLS certificate.

apiClientNoAccess.message: Requestion has no host permission for $1. Without it, the browser blocks the response (CORS).

apiClientHostNotAllowed.message: The organization policy blocks requests to $1.

apiClientHistoryHint.message: The last $1 sent requests appear here. Requests are stored as entered (with {{variables}}, without their values).
apiClientHistoryHint.description: $1 is the number of requests the history keeps.

apiClientHistoryClearText.message: All requests will be deleted from the history. Open tabs are not affected.

apiClientHistoryActionFailed.message: Failed to update the history. Try again.

apiClientMissingVariables.message: No values for variables: $1. Select an environment that defines them, or add them to the current one.
apiClientMissingVariables.description: $1 is a comma-separated list of variable names.

apiClientEnvironmentsEmpty.message: An environment stores variable values (for example, {{baseUrl}} or {{token}}) for a single stage. Select the active environment in the page header.

apiClientEnvironmentEditNamed.description: $1 is the name of an environment.

apiClientEnvironmentDeleteNamed.description: $1 is the name of an environment.

apiClientEnvironmentsActionFailed.message: Failed to update the environments. Try again.

apiClientEnvironmentSaveFailed.description: $1 is the technical reason, in English.

apiClientEnvironmentDeleteText.message: The environment “$1” and its variables will be permanently deleted.

apiClientVariableEncrypted.message: Encrypted (enter a new value to replace)

apiClientVariablesHint.message: Variable syntax: {{name}}. Supported in the URL, params, headers and body.

apiClientSecretsWarning.message: Secret values are masked in the UI but stored unencrypted in the browser profile. To encrypt them with a master password, use the button in the page header.

apiClientVaultRequiredWarning.message: The organization policy requires secret encryption. Values of variables marked Secret are not saved until encryption is turned on.

apiClientSecretsEncrypted.message: Secret values are encrypted with the master password and are not shown in the editor. Enter a new value to replace one.

apiClientSecretsLocked.message: The vault is locked, so these encrypted variables have no value: $1. Unlock the vault in the page header.
apiClientSecretsLocked.description: $1 is a comma-separated list of variable names.

apiClientVaultRequired.message: The organization policy requires secret encryption. Turn on encryption to use $1.
apiClientVaultRequired.description: $1 is a list of variable names.

apiClientVaultChangeText.message: Secret values will be re-encrypted with a key derived from the new password.

apiClientVaultFailed.message: The vault is not responding. Try again.

apiClientVaultSetupText.message: Secret values in all environments will be encrypted with a key derived from the master password (PBKDF2). The password itself is not stored.

apiClientVaultSetupWarning.message: Password recovery is not possible. If the password is lost, encrypted values can only be deleted (vault reset) and entered again.

apiClientVaultAutoLockHint.message: The vault locks automatically after $1 min of inactivity and when the browser closes.

apiClientVaultUnlockText.message: Enter the master password to use encrypted values in requests.

apiClientVaultDisableText.message: Secret values will be decrypted and stored unencrypted in the browser profile. Enter the master password to confirm.

apiClientVaultResetText.message: Encrypted values will be deleted and encryption turned off. Variables are kept with empty values that must be entered again.

apiClientVaultLockedSave.message: The vault is locked. Unlock it in the page header to save secret values.

apiClientVaultRequiredSave.message: The organization policy requires secret encryption. Turn on encryption and save again.

apiClientCurlCommandHint.message: For example, from DevTools → Copy as cURL (bash). The request opens in a new tab. cmd and PowerShell syntax is not supported.

apiClientCurlCommandPlaceholder.description: An example command; keep it as is.

apiClientCurlImportFailed.description: $1 is the technical reason, in English.

apiClientCurlExportSecretsHint.message: When unchecked, secrets stay as {{name}} and do not end up in the clipboard.

apiClientCurlExportMissing.message: Variables without values are left as is: $1.
apiClientCurlExportMissing.description: $1 is a comma-separated list of variable names.

apiClientCurlExportCookies.message: Browser cookies are not included in the command. If the server requires them, add a Cookie header.

apiClientCurlExportCopyFailed.message: Failed to copy. Select the command and copy it manually.

apiClientCollectionsEmpty.message: Request storage in collections and folders. Ctrl+S saves the current tab's request.

apiClientCollectionMenu.description: $1 is the name of a collection, a folder or a request.

apiClientCollectionDeleteText.message: “$1” will be deleted (with all contents, if it is a folder or a collection). Requests in open tabs are kept.
apiClientCollectionDeleteText.description: $1 is the name of a collection, a folder or a request.

apiClientImportHint.message: Supported formats (JSON, up to 10 MB): Postman collection (v2.0, v2.1), Postman environment, OpenAPI 3.0 or 3.1 specification.

apiClientImportCollection.description: $1 is a name, $2 and $3 are numbers.

apiClientImportEnvironment.message: New environment “$1” (variables: $2). Select it in the page header to use its variables.
apiClientImportEnvironment.description: $1 is a name, $2 is a number.

apiClientImportSecretsPlain.message: Secret values will be stored unencrypted. To encrypt them, turn on encryption in the page header before importing.

apiClientImportSecretsEncrypted.message: Secret values will be encrypted with the master password.

apiClientImportSecretsLocked.message: The vault is locked, so secret values will not be imported. Unlock the vault in the page header and import again.

apiClientImportSecretsRequired.message: The organization policy requires secret encryption, so secret values will not be imported. Turn on encryption and import again.

apiClientImportGapScripts.message: Scripts and tests (scripts: $2): code from the file is never executed

apiClientImportGapBodies.message: Body modes $1 (requests: $2): only JSON, text and x-www-form-urlencoded forms are supported
apiClientImportGapBodies.description: $1 is a list of body modes, $2 is a number.

apiClientImportGapBodiesOfBodyless.message: Bodies of $1 requests (requests: $2): requests with these methods are sent without a body
apiClientImportGapBodiesOfBodyless.description: $1 is a list of methods, $2 is a number.

apiClientImportGapAuths.description: $1 is a list of authorization types, $2 is a number.

apiClientImportGapBasicWithVariables.message: Basic authorization with {{variables}} (requests: $2): credentials are Base64-encoded, so variables cannot be substituted

apiClientImportGapMethods.message: Requests with methods $1 (requests: $2): these methods are not supported
apiClientImportGapMethods.description: $1 is a list of methods, $2 is a number.

apiClientImportGapDynamicVariables.message: Dynamic variables $1 (requests: $2): not supported, left as is
apiClientImportGapDynamicVariables.description: $1 is a list of templates, $2 is a number.

apiClientImportGapDeepFolders.message: Folders nested deeper than five levels (folders: $2): their requests are moved to the fifth-level folder

apiClientImportGapVariableNames.message: Variables with names not allowed in the {{name}} syntax: $1

apiClientImportEmptySecrets.message: Before sending requests, set these secret values in the environment: $1.

apiClientImportGapRelativeServer.message: Relative server URL $1: set the full API URL in the environment's baseUrl variable

apiClientImportGapExternalRefs.message: External references $1 (references: $2): only references within the file are supported
apiClientImportGapExternalRefs.description: $1 is a list of references, $2 is a number.

apiClientImportGapCookieParameters.description: $1 is a list of names, $2 is a number.

apiClientImportGapOwnServers.message: Operations with their own servers field (requests: $2): sent to baseUrl like the rest

apiClientImportVariablesSuffix.description: Ends the name of the environment made of the variables of a collection.

dialogClose.description: Accessible name of the button that closes a dialog.
